title: The Chair Kept Empty: a Basel Hebraist, the Morning Land, and the House That Talked to the Dead
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Rümlingen, born in the parsonage
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In the Reformed parsonage of Rümlingen, a village of the Basel countryside where the Homburgertal narrows, the pastor Alexander Preiswerk and his wife have a son on the nineteenth of September. They name him Samuel. The surname is an old Basel one, but this branch of it lives on a country stipend. He will spend nearly the whole of his life inside a circle ten kilometres wide around the city downstream, and where in that circle he lies buried is nowhere recorded. His first schoolroom is his father's study.
stops.quote: Preiswerk: Samuel P., Dichter geistlicher Lieder, wurde geboren am 19. September 1799 als Sohn des reformirten Pfarrers Alexander P. zu Rümlingen in Baselland.
stops.quote_source: Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie, vol. 26 (Duncker & Humblot, Leipzig, 1888), p. 552
suggested_refs: The Reformed parsonage and church of Rümlingen, Basel-Landschaft

stops.name: Basel, the old college above the Rhine
stops.date_confidence: inferred; no matriculation year appears in ADB or in either Wikipedia article, and the widely repeated 1818 is unsourced
stops.campa: Prepared by his father, he matriculates at Basel and reads theology in the old college above the Rhine, the Untere Kollegium at the Rheinsprung, where the university has sat since 1460 and will sit until the Kollegienhaus opens at Petersplatz in 1939. No source read gives the year he entered. The faculty is small, orthodox and short of students; Hebrew is taught in it as a service to exegesis rather than as a subject with a life of its own. A Basel theologian's course in these years assumes a season or two abroad. He does not stay.
suggested_refs: The Alte Universität at Rheinsprung 9, seat of the University of Basel until 1939

stops.name: Tübingen, the university that fell out of the accounts
stops.date_confidence: inferred; ADB names the sequence Basel, Tübingen, Erlangen and dates none of the three. The year here is a position in the order, not a record
stops.campa: Between Basel and Erlangen he studies at Tübingen. The Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie names all three universities in a single clause; German Wikipedia omits Tübingen altogether, which is how the stop went missing from nearly every later account of him. He comes out of his student decade a Hebraist who reads the prophets as reportage about a country still on the map. What he heard at Tübingen is unrecorded, and the matriculation registers of the university were not consulted here.
stops.quote: Durch seinen Vater dazu vorbereitet, bezog er die Universität Basel und studirte hier und hernach auch in Tübingen und Erlangen Theologie.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the University of Tübingen, c. 1818-1821, unconsulted

stops.name: Erlangen, the fraternity that changed its name
stops.date_confidence: attested to the winter semester 1821/22; the month is the opening of that semester, not a recorded date
stops.campa: In the winter semester of 1821/22 the Swiss theology student joins the Erlanger Burschenschaft, the nationalist fraternity founded four years before as the Allgemeine Erlanger Burschenschaft. A foreigner sworn into a German patriotic society in these years is a police matter. It will not be called the Bubenreuther until after the dissolution of 1833, when the survivors take the name of the village outside town where they had met; the fraternity histories that list Preiswerk among their notable members list him under that later name, which nobody used while he was there.
suggested_refs: Ernst Höhne, Die Bubenreuther II (Erlangen 1936), p. 70
Helge Dvorak, Biographisches Lexikon der Deutschen Burschenschaft II (Heidelberg 2018), pp. 547-548

stops.name: Benken, the vicariate
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: Home from Erlangen at twenty-two, he takes the vicariate at Biel-Benken, two villages grown into one on the road toward the French border, and preaches his first sermons to farmers. The pin sits on the Benken half of the pair. It is the lowest rung of the Reformed ladder in the canton and the ordinary first posting for a pastor's son. The record for the year runs to a single fact, that he held the office. Nothing survives of what he said from that pulpit.
suggested_refs: The Reformed parish church of Benken, Basel-Landschaft

stops.name: Basel, chaplain to the orphanage
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: He is called into the city as pastor of the Waisenhaus, chaplain to Basel's orphaned children. Which building the orphanage occupied in the 1820s could not be fixed in any source read here; the pin is the centre of the old city and not the house itself. The post is a stepping stone and everyone involved knows it: no parish, no tithe, a salary and a pulpit and the standing to be considered for something better. He marries in the same year. His wife is Charlotte Hopf.
suggested_refs: The Basel Waisenhaus of the 1820s, premises unidentified

stops.name: Basel, the death of Charlotte Hopf
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the Personenlexikon Baselland; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: Charlotte Preiswerk-Hopf dies within a year of the wedding. Nothing is recorded of the cause, and nothing of her beyond the two dates. Every later story told about this household begins from this death. What is documented is a marriage in 1824 and a death in 1825, both in the Personenlexikon of Basel-Landschaft. What follows in the family accounts is memory carried forward by his descendants and written down, three generations later, by biographers of his grandson.
suggested_refs: Basel civil and parish registers for the Preiswerk household, 1824-1826, unconsulted

stops.name: Basel, the chair kept for her
stops.date_confidence: undated tradition; the year is placed at the second marriage because the story requires a second wife to be dismayed by it
stops.campa: Family tradition holds that he sets aside one day of every week for conversation with Charlotte's spirit and keeps a chair for her in his study, which she is said to visit often. In 1826 he marries Augusta Faber, who lives out her married life alongside the arrangement and, the tradition adds, does not care for it. No letter, diary or parish document supporting any of this was located here. The story reaches print through the literature on his grandson, above all Deirdre Bair. Whether Augusta ever said so herself, the record does not show.
suggested_refs: Deirdre Bair, Jung: A Biography (Little, Brown, 2003), p. 72
sources: Jung biographical tradition (Bair 2003; Ellenberger 1970), unverified at first hand
Personenlexikon Baselland, 'Samuel Preiswerk', for the two marriages

stops.name: Basel, the Hebrew class at the Mission House
stops.date_confidence: disputed: ADB gives 1829 and names Hebrew as the subject, German Wikipedia gives 1828 and says only that he taught. Month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: He is appointed teacher of Hebrew at the Missionshaus, the seminary of the Basel Mission that trains evangelists for the Gold Coast and the Malabar shore. Until now he has been a curate and a chaplain; here the language is his subject. The two sources disagree by a year, 1828 against 1829, and by a detail: ADB names Hebrew and German Wikipedia names no subject at all. The pin is the Missionsstrasse house, which is where the mission stands later and may not be where it stood in his time.
suggested_refs: Basel Mission archive, seminary teaching records for the late 1820s

stops.name: Basel, the hymn that outlived the scholarship
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month unrecorded and set arbitrarily within it
stops.campa: In the mission-house years he writes 'Die Sach ist dein, Herr Jesu Christ.' Sixteen more of his hymns circulate first in manuscript among friends, and nine will be taken into Albert Knapp's Liederschatz in 1850, which in the German-speaking churches of that century is how a hymn passes into general use. The Hebrew grammar is the work he is proud of. The hymn from the mission house is still in print: number 801 in the Swiss Reformed Gesangbuch, 593 in the Württemberg Evangelisches Gesangbuch, 427 in a Mennonite hymnal.
suggested_refs: Reformiertes Gesangbuch 801; Evangelisches Gesangbuch Württemberg 593

stops.name: Muttenz, the parish under the Wartenberg
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: He is given the parish of Muttenz, a substantial village under the three ruined castles of the Wartenberg, with its ring-walled churchyard and its fortified church of St Arbogast. It is a real living at last: land, a congregation, a house. He arrives in the year the Basel countryside begins to move in earnest against the city that governs it, and he takes the city's side, which in a Baselbiet pulpit is not a position a man can hold quietly. The village will be a separate canton from his employers within three years.
suggested_refs: The fortified church of St Arbogast at Muttenz with its ring wall

stops.name: Muttenz, driven from the parsonage
stops.date_confidence: year attested by ADB; German Wikipedia gives only 'soon after' 1830. Month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: The Basel-Landschaft rising reaches Muttenz. Asked to speak prayers favourable to the revolutionary cause, he refuses, and is driven out. Accounts written from his grandson's side of the family have long glossed this as the French July Revolution of 1830; ADB is unambiguous that the revolution in question broke out in Baselland and that the expulsion falls in 1832. The July Revolution version turns a local quarrel about who governs a valley into a stand against Paris. He is thirty-two, with a second wife and children, and no post.
suggested_refs: The Baselbieter Wirren and the 1833 separation of Basel-Landschaft from Basel-Stadt

stops.name: Basel, two years of private lessons
stops.date_confidence: the interval 1832-1834 is attested by ADB; the month is arbitrary and the location is inference, since no source says where the family lodged
stops.campa: For two years he keeps himself and his family, in ADB's word kümmerlich, meagrely, by private tutoring. No parish, no chair, no journal, no stipend. Where the household lived between 1832 and 1834 is not recorded in anything read here; the pin is Basel because that is where paying pupils would have been. The interval is missing from every summary that runs his church posts together as a smooth ascent, and it is the only period in which he is documented as poor.
stops.quote: Aus dieser Stellung wurde er im J. 1832 bei der in Baselland ausgebrochenen Revolution verjagt; er ernährte sich und die Seinen kümmerlich durch Privatunterricht, bis er im J. 1834 als außerordentlicher Professor der alttestamentlichen Exegese und der orientalischen Sprachen an die École de Théologie der evangelischen Gesellschaft in Genf gerufen ward.
suggested_refs: Basel household and tax records, 1832-1834, unconsulted

stops.name: Geneva, the school of the Evangelical Society
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: The Evangelical Society of Geneva calls him as professor extraordinarius of Old Testament exegesis and the oriental languages. Its École de Théologie is a creation of the Réveil, founded to train pastors outside a Genevan state church its founders consider doctrinally dead. Where the school kept its premises in these years is not established in any source read here; the pin marks the old town. At thirty-five he crosses the language line and lectures on the Hebrew Bible in French.
suggested_refs: The École de Théologie of the Société évangélique de Genève, premises unidentified

stops.name: Geneva, the Grammaire hébraïque
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the sources place the grammar in the Geneva years without giving a publication date
stops.campa: He writes a Hebrew grammar in French. The Grammaire hébraïque runs to four editions and becomes the thing his name is attached to in scholarly catalogues for the rest of the century, ahead of the hymns and the journal both. Two years after being chased out of a village parsonage in the Baselbiet, a country pastor's son is the man Genevan students learn their paradigms from. No copy of any of the four editions was consulted here, and the year of the first is nowhere stated in the sources read.
suggested_refs: Samuel Preiswerk, Grammaire hébraïque, four editions

stops.name: Geneva, the company of Edward Irving's men
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the sources attest the contact and its consequence in 1837 but give no date for its beginning
stops.campa: Representatives of Edward Irving's Catholic Apostolic movement are in Geneva, and Preiswerk keeps their company. Irvingite preaching turns on the imminent return of Christ, on restored apostles, on prophecy spoken aloud in the congregation. The Evangelical Society, itself a movement of revival, regards all of that as fanaticism and tells him to choose. What the association cost him is documented. No source read here records what he found in these men, or what he said when he was told to drop them.
suggested_refs: The Catholic Apostolic Church and its restorationist eschatology

stops.name: Geneva, the second post lost to a refusal
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: He is told to break with the Irvingians and will not, and the Evangelical Society dismisses him three years after calling him. The Geneva interlude closes; he recrosses the language line to Basel with nothing waiting for him there. It is the second time in five years that a refusal to say what he is asked to say has cost him a salary, and the second time he lands in Basel with a family and no employer. No minute of the Society's decision was read here, and his own account of the break, if he wrote one, has not been found.
stops.quote: Seeking to maintain his connection with representatives of Edward Irving his job was lost in 1837.
stops.quote_source: English Wikipedia, 'Samuel Preiswerk' (raw wikitext; the sentence carries no page-level citation there)
suggested_refs: Minutes of the Société évangélique de Genève for 1837, unconsulted

stops.name: Basel, the monthly begun out of unemployment
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1838 by ADB; the day is defaulted
stops.campa: Out of work again, he starts a monthly. 'Das Morgenland: Altes und Neues für Freunde der Heiligen Schrift', the morning land, old things and new for friends of Holy Scripture, begins appearing in June. It is made for readers who want the Bible's world handled as a real geography with a present tense: the land, its peoples, its languages, what is happening there now. He edits it, writes much of it and publishes it, from a city that has not offered him a pulpit. The editorial address is not recorded.
stops.quote: In der stellungslosen Zeit gab P. eine Monatsschrift heraus, deren Inhalt sich aus dem Titel ergibt: 'Das Morgenland, Altes und Neues für Freunde der heiligen Schrift'.
suggested_refs: Das Morgenland, six annual volumes, Basel 1838-1843

stops.name: Basel, Palestine argued in a small monthly
stops.date_confidence: the position is attested for the run 1838-1843 as a whole; no individual article or date is identified in any source read
stops.campa: In the pages of Das Morgenland he argues that the Jews should return to Palestine and settle it. The Personenlexikon Baselland states it without ceremony: in the journal he supported the idea of the settlement of Palestine by the Jews. A University of Basel repository record calls him a Basel forerunner of Zionism who argued theologically for a return to the land in the 1830s and 1840s. He is a Reformed pastor with no parish and no chair, writing in a monthly of small circulation. Nobody has quoted a sentence of his own on the subject.
suggested_refs: Personenlexikon Baselland, 'Samuel Preiswerk'
University of Basel repository record, 'ein Basler Vorläufer des Zionismus'

stops.name: Basel, the six volumes close
stops.date_confidence: year attested; ADB counts six annual volumes from June 1838, against the five-year run usually reported. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The journal stops. ADB counts six annual volumes from June 1838, a longer run than the five years usually credited to it. In the same year its editor is given back a pulpit and a lectern. Wikisource catalogues the title among periodicals of Judaica, which is the nearest thing to an outside judgment of its subject matter located here. No complete set was read for this account and not one of its articles is quoted. What the six volumes say about Palestine, at what length and on what argument, the surviving copies could answer and this account cannot.
stops.quote: Es erschienen sechs Jahrgänge vom Juni 1838 bis zum Jahre 1843.
suggested_refs: Surviving runs of Das Morgenland in Swiss and German library holdings

stops.name: Basel, sixteen hymns published without his name
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: Two friends collect sixteen of his hymns and bring them out anonymously in the 'Evangelischer Liederkranz aus älterer und neuerer Zeit' at Basel. His name is on none of it. One of the sixteen, 'Dies ist der Gemeine Stärke', will be turned into English by Catherine Winkworth for the second series of her Lyra Germanica in 1858, sung as 'Hark, the Church Proclaims Her Honour', and carried from there into a Bedford hymnal and then the Ohio Lutheran Hymnal of 1880.
stops.quote: Von seinen geistlichen Liedern hatten mehrere schon in Privatkreisen Verbreitung und Anerkennung gefunden, als zwei seiner Freunde sie in dem von ihnen anonym herausgegebenen 'Evangelischen Liederkranz aus älterer und neuerer Zeit' (Basel 1844) weiteren Kreisen zugänglich machten.
suggested_refs: Catherine Winkworth, Lyra Germanica, second series (1858)
Ohio Lutheran Hymnal (1880)

stops.name: Basel, the lectureship and the licentiate
stops.date_confidence: disputed and left disputed: German Wikipedia gives 1839 for a lectureship in Hebrew language and literature, ADB gives 1843 for a Privatdozentur in Old Testament exegesis bundled with the licentiate and the parish. ADB's date is used for the pin
stops.campa: He is made licentiate of theology and Privatdozent, and lectures again in the old precinct above the Rhine where he had been a student twenty-five years earlier. The two sources contradict each other about when and about what: German Wikipedia has a lectureship in Hebrew language and literature in 1839, ADB has a Privatdozentur in Old Testament exegesis in 1843, tied in one clause to the licentiate and the parish. Family tradition adds that he had learned Hebrew in the belief that it is the language spoken in heaven.
suggested_refs: University of Basel faculty registers for the 1840s, unconsulted
sources: Jung biographical tradition, for the language of heaven

stops.name: Basel, pastor of St Leonhard
stops.date_confidence: disputed: German Wikipedia gives 1840, ADB gives 1843. ADB is preferred here because its own arithmetic, sixteen years at St Leonhard ending in the undisputed 1859 election, works only from 1843. The month is arbitrary
stops.campa: He becomes pastor of St Leonhard on the terrace above the Kohlenberg and holds the parish sixteen years, eleven years after he was living on private lessons. The count of sixteen is ADB's own, and it is the reason for preferring ADB's start date: sixteen years from 1843 reaches the Münster election of 1859 exactly, and sixteen from Wikipedia's 1840 reaches nothing. The church is a former Augustinian foundation, a late Gothic nave standing over a Romanesque crypt cut into the hill.
suggested_refs: The Leonhardskirche and its Romanesque crypt, Basel

stops.name: Basel, the address spoken over him
stops.date_confidence: the pamphlet is dated 1845; the day of the installation is not recorded in any source read
stops.campa: At his installation an address is spoken over him and afterwards printed: 'Die Einsegnung des Herrn Samuel Preiswerk', containing an Einsegnungsrede by Jacob Burckhardt. That name has been read as the art historian's, which is almost certainly wrong. The Burckhardt who blesses a new Basel pastor in 1845 is Jakob Burckhardt the elder, head of the Münster congregation since 1838 and Antistes of the Basel clergy, holder of the office Preiswerk will take over in fourteen years. The pamphlet itself was not read for this account.
suggested_refs: Die Einsegnung des Herrn Samuel Preiswerk (Basel, 1845), unread

stops.name: Basel, the birth of Emilie
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: His youngest child is born and named Emilie. She grows up in a parsonage where the dead are spoken of as present company, and by her own family's account of her she becomes two women: a pastor's wife of the ordinary kind in daylight, and at night one who says that spirits come into her bedroom. She will marry a Hebrew student of her father's, follow him into a country parsonage of the same kind her father was born in, and in 1875, four years after Samuel is in the ground, bear that student a son.
suggested_refs: Emilie Preiswerk-Jung, 1848-1923

stops.name: Basel, the daughter set behind his chair
stops.date_confidence: undated tradition; the year is placed when Emilie is old enough to sit still, and rests on no record
stops.campa: The tradition the Jung family kept about this house has the old man writing his sermons with the child Emilie seated behind him, put there so that the spirits could not come at his back while he worked. The detail is transmitted separately from the story of the chair kept for Charlotte and points the same way. Neither appears in any document contemporary with him. Both come out of the record his grandson's biographers made, and not out of the Basel church archives.
suggested_refs: Deirdre Bair, Jung: A Biography (2003), p. 72
sources: Jung biographical tradition (Bair 2003), unverified at first hand

stops.name: Basel, teaching Paul Achilles Jung his Hebrew
stops.date_confidence: undated; no source read gives a year for the coursework. The date here is a placement between Paul Jung's likely student years and the marriage, and is not a record
stops.campa: Among the theology students taking Hebrew from him is Johann Paul Achilles Jung, son of Carl Gustav Jung the elder, the Basel professor of medicine whom the city holds to be a natural son of Goethe. No source read here gives a year for the coursework; the placing of it is a guess between Paul's student years and his wedding. Paul takes a doctorate in oriental languages, finds no place in the field, becomes a country pastor, and stops reading. He marries his old teacher's daughter Emilie.
suggested_refs: Johann Paul Achilles Jung's dissertation in oriental languages, Basel

stops.name: Basel, elected to the Münster and to the office
stops.date_confidence: year attested by ADB, German Wikipedia and French Wikipedia alike; month and day unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: After sixteen years at St Leonhard he is elected to the Münster, and with the Münster comes the office of Antistes, head of the Reformed clergy of the city. It is the summit of the Basel church, and it makes him the first officer of a city whose clergy his own father served as a village pastor forty miles upstream. He reaches it at sixty, thirty-seven years after the vicariate at Benken and twenty-seven after being run out of Muttenz for declining to pray as instructed. The man who blessed him into St Leonhard in 1845 held this office before him. He holds it until he dies.
stops.quote: Nachdem er 16 Jahre zu St. Leonhard gestanden, wurde er im Jahre 1859 als Antistes der Baseler Kirche an den Münster gewählt. Er starb am 13. Januar 1871.
suggested_refs: The Basler Münster and the office of Antistes

stops.name: Basel, the church and the schools together
stops.date_confidence: the office runs 1859-1871; this pin marks the administration rather than a dated event
stops.campa: The Antistes of Basel is not only a churchman. The office carries oversight of the city's church and its schools as one system, the two having never been pulled apart here, so that the man in the Münster pulpit also answers for what the children of the republic are taught. Where his administrative office physically stood was not established for this file; the pin is the Rathaus on the Marktplatz, seat of the civil authority he worked beside for twelve years.
suggested_refs: The Antistitium of Basel, premises unidentified

stops.name: Basel, the honorary doctorate
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month unrecorded and set arbitrarily within it
stops.campa: The university gives him an honorary doctorate in theology, four decades after he left it as a student bound for Tübingen. The Deutsche Biographie portal files him under six occupations: Antistes of the Basel church, sacred poet, pastor, grammar-school teacher, theologian, writer. Palestine is not among the six words, and the household is not either. The grammar-school post appears in no other source read here. Where he kept a school, and in which years, nothing says.
stops.quote: 1799 – 1871, Antistes der Basler Kirche; geistlicher Dichter; Pfarrer; Gymnasiallehrer; Theologe; Schriftsteller
suggested_refs: University of Basel honorary doctorate records, 1860

stops.name: Basel, death of the Antistes
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He dies in Basel on the thirteenth of January, seventy-one years old, Antistes for eleven of those years and a pastor of the city or the countryside for most of the rest. Augusta outlives him. Emilie is twenty-two and not yet married, and will not meet the man she marries for some years yet. The family says he kept up the weekly conversations for forty-five years with a woman who died in 1825; nobody in the house wrote down a word of what passed in them. No account of the funeral or the estate mentions the chair.
suggested_refs: Basel death register, 13 January 1871

stops.name: Basel, the grave that was not found
stops.date_confidence: gap: no burial date, site, stone or plaque is recorded in any source reachable for this account. The date is a placeholder a week after death and carries no authority
stops.campa: No burial place is recorded for him in anything reachable here. Not a churchyard, not a stone, not a plaque, not a funeral notice. The Historisches Lexikon der Schweiz holds an article on him, number 10790, written by a Peter A. Preiswerk, and it refused every attempt to fetch it with a 403. The Kirchenlexikon article by Hans Fritzsche survives in an archived copy that has not been read. Where is the Antistes of Basel buried? The two works most likely to say were not opened for this account.
suggested_refs: HLS article 10790, 'Preiswerk, Samuel', by Peter A. Preiswerk, inaccessible
BBKL vol. 7, cols. 923-925, by Hans Fritzsche, unread archived copy
sources: Gap recorded after failed retrieval of HLS (HTTP 403) and BBKL

stops.name: Kesswil, the grandson born four years late
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In the parsonage at Kesswil on the flat shore of Lake Constance, Emilie Preiswerk bears Paul Jung a son. Samuel has been dead four years and the boy never sees him, which does not stop him growing up on the subject: the Hebraist in Basel who kept a chair for a ghost, the mother who heard voices at night, a house where the presence of the dead was a domestic arrangement and not a doctrine. They name the boy Carl Gustav, after the other grandfather, the physician.
suggested_refs: The Kesswil parsonage on Lake Constance

stops.name: Basel, the voice at the table
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the sittings run 1894 or 1895 to 1899 depending on the source, and the day is the one already carried in the family account
stops.campa: In a Preiswerk house in the city, his fifteen-year-old kinswoman Helly falls into trance at the table and speaks in the voice of dead grandfather Samuel Preiswerk. How she descends from him could not be established from any genealogy read for this file; what is on record is the name the family gave the voice. Her cousin Carl Gustav Jung, a medical student, attends the Saturday sittings until 1899 and writes it all down: the somnambulisms, the cosmology drawn in circles, the personalities forming and dissolving.
suggested_refs: Helene Preiswerk's mandala cosmology diagram
Preiswerk family circle

stops.name: Basel, the congress in the Stadtcasino
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Theodor Herzl convenes the First Zionist Congress in the concert hall of the Stadtcasino. Twenty-six years earlier the head of this city's Reformed clergy had argued in a Basel monthly that the Jews should settle Palestine. Henri Ellenberger thought the coincidence of city no coincidence at all. Nothing links the two men: Herzl came to Basel because Munich's Jewish community had refused him a venue, and no delegate in that hall is recorded as ever having heard the name Preiswerk.
suggested_refs: The Stadtcasino concert hall at Basel, seat of the early Zionist Congresses
sources: Henri Ellenberger, The Discovery of the Unconscious (1970), as reported in secondary summary and not read at first hand

stops.name: Zurich, the séances become a thesis
stops.date_confidence: the thesis is dated 1902 by German Wikipedia and given as published 1903 by English Wikipedia; both are correct for different acts and the confusion between them is common. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Jung submits a doctoral thesis on the young medium his cousin Hélène and the sittings he had recorded in Basel. It is defended in 1902 and printed in 1903, and the two dates are routinely run together as one. The family habit of holding the dead present in the room, which began, if the tradition is right, with a chair left empty for Charlotte Hopf in 1826, has become a clinical case history and the opening move of a career in psychiatry. What the grandfather did as devotion the grandson writes up under the title Zur Psychologie und Pathologie sogenannter occulter Phänomene.
stops.quote: Influenced by an earlier study by Freud's contemporary Théodore Flournoy, Jung wrote his doctoral thesis on spiritualism, focusing on a young medium, his cousin Hélène Preiswerk, whose séances and table turnings he had attended.

stops.name: Küsnacht, the last of his children
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the family accounts give January 1923 without a fixed day
stops.campa: Emilie Preiswerk-Jung dies suddenly in January, seventy-five years old, the youngest and last of Samuel's children. She had been the child seated behind the writing desk to keep the spirits off her father's back, and the woman who said they came into her bedroom at night. The night before the news reaches her son he dreams of a dark primeval wood and hears Wotan's hunt go over to fetch one of its own. He records the grief, and running underneath it something he cannot account for, an undertone like the marriage-dance of the dead.
